title: Chevrolet K5 Blazer Engines by Year
description: Every factory engine in the full-size Chevrolet K5 Blazer by year, 1969–1994: the 250 six, the 307, 350 and 400 V8s, the 305, and the 6.2 and 6.5 diesels.
intro: The full-size Blazer was built on the C/K pickup from 1969 to 1994; it was sold with two-wheel drive as well until 1982. For 1995 it was renamed the Tahoe. The compact S-10 Blazer is a different vehicle.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Blazer offered the 250 six and the 307 and 350 V8s. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.

The second Blazer added the 400 V8 for 1975–1979, the 305 from 1977, and GM's 6.2 diesel from 1982; the six was dropped after 1982. Several ratings differ from the pickup's because the Blazer often carried heavy-duty emissions equipment.
The GMT400 Blazer used the 5.7 V8, with a 6.5 turbo diesel for 1994.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
